- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects with a lag — model lags behind true trend reversals.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to prior averages too quickly, missing sustained momentum.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility; model reacts too aggressively to short-term noise, leading to overfitting.
- When true prices show a clear upward trend, model often underestimates the magnitude of the rise, especially in the final 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits “early peak” bias — forecasts peak too soon, then drop too early, missing the true peak or late rally.
- Forecasts are generally too smooth — fail to capture sudden, sharp price jumps or corrections that occur in the last 5–7 days.
